subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what trigger plus local editor/temp-file safety contract should it use?
rationale: The implementation surface is clear, but choosing a global shortcut or slash command and defining safe local process and temporary-file behavior requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve guarded core flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold for UX/security spec
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers choose the shortcut or slash-command model and resolve the inactive external-editor keybinding mismatch.

options.title: Decline external process handoff
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers prefer inline multiline editing, composer expansion, or another non-process workflow.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded core flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this issue and is the strongest routing signal for the TUI product and security tradeoff.
